key_insight: A stoichiometry-preserved ionic-cluster representation, combined with pretrained MLIPs and multi-task fine-tuning, can predict detonation performance of multi-ionic energetic materials before full crystal structures are available.
engineering_relevance: This offers a synthesis-facing screening route for data-scarce multi-ionic materials, reducing reliance on exhaustive crystal-structure prediction and accelerating candidate prioritization.
method: Represent each candidate as a non-periodic stoichiometric ionic cluster rather than a full periodic crystal.
Fine-tune a pretrained atomistic MLIP with multi-task energy-force objectives to regularize sparse property labels.
Use the learned surrogate to screen new ABX4 energetic materials, including unseen stoichiometry and cation chemistry.
evidence_signal: On 25 curated perovskite-type energetic materials with experimental Kamlet–Jacobs detonation velocities, the surrogate achieved cross-validated screening and transferred to three newly synthesized ABX4 compounds with a mean absolute error of 92 m/s.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and coverage of the pretrained backbone and the small curated training set, so extrapolation beyond similar multi-ionic chemistries should be treated cautiously.
paper_title: Stoichiometric cluster learning for few-shot property prediction of multi-ionic integrated energetic materials
